chunks: And faces, on that Day, will be dust-begrimed.

key_terms.غَبَرَةٌ: Dust or dirt covering the face

ai.seo_question: What does it mean for faces to be 'dust-begrimed' on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse (98:4) is often interpreted through the lens of *al-Ghubbah* (dust/dirt) as a physical manifestation of the spiritual stagnation resulting from the rejection of the Prophet and the Imams. It serves as a stark counterpoint to the luminous faces of the *Mu'minun*, emphasizing that true nobility is derived from adherence to divine authority (*Wilayah*) rather than worldly status.
